title: "Resources"

## Getting help

-   **In R:** type `?function_name` in the Console (for example `?mutate`) to open its help page.
-   **Setup problems:** see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd) for installing Rtools (Windows) and the Xcode Command Line Tools and gfortran (Mac).
-   **During the workshop:** put up your red sticky note!

## Free books and guides

-   **[R for Data Science (2e)](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/)** — the standard introduction to the tidyverse, by the people who wrote it. Free online.
-   **[The Epidemiologist R Handbook](https://epirhandbook.com/)** — hundreds of applied examples for public health, using the same packages as this workshop. The workshop's outbreak dataset is based on its example linelist.
-   **[Data Carpentry: R for Social Scientists](https://datacarpentry.github.io/r-socialsci/)** and **[R for Ecologists](https://datacarpentry.github.io/R-ecology-lesson/)** — other beginner R lessons in the same hands-on style.

## Base R and the tidyverse

-   **[Base R ↔ tidyverse](base-vs-tidyverse.qmd)** — this workshop's translation table: every tidyverse function we use, its base R equivalent, and what to watch out for.
-   **[Advanced R: Subsetting and Vectors](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/)** — when you want to understand vectors, lists, and `[[ ]]` in depth.

## Cheat sheets

Posit's one-page cheat sheets are great to keep open while you work: [all cheat sheets](https://posit.co/resources/cheatsheets/). The most useful for this workshop:

-   **Data transformation with dplyr** — Sessions 1–5
-   **Data tidying with tidyr** — Session 4
-   **Data visualization with ggplot2** — Sessions 6–7
-   **Factors with forcats**, **Strings with stringr**, **Dates and times with lubridate**
-   **Apply functions with purrr** — Session 8
-   **Base R** — vectors, lists, indexing, and the apply family (in the "Contributed" section of the cheat sheet page)

## Packages used in the workshop

| Package | What we use it for |
|---|---|
| [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/) | dplyr (wrangling), ggplot2 (plots), tidyr (reshaping), stringr, forcats, lubridate, purrr |
| [here](https://here.r-lib.org/) | file paths that work on any computer |
| [rio](https://gesistsa.github.io/rio/) | `import()` and `export()` for almost any file type |
| [janitor](https://sfirke.github.io/janitor/) | `clean_names()`, `tabyl()`, `get_dupes()` |
| [skimr](https://docs.ropensci.org/skimr/) | `skim()` summaries |
| [gtsummary](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/) | publication-ready tables |
| [scales](https://scales.r-lib.org/) | formatting percentages |
